title: Paphlagonia
capsule: Paphlagonia was a region and sometimes independent kingdom along the central Black Sea coast of Anatolia, hemmed between the Bithynians to the west and the Pontic kingdom to the east. Its native Paphlagonian dynasty maintained a degree of autonomy under Achaemenid suzerainty in the fifth century BCE, and after Alexander's conquests it briefly reasserted independence under rulers such as Morzius. Mithridates V of Pontus annexed the territory around 120 BCE, and it was subsequently organized as a Roman province in 6 BCE under Augustus, ending Paphlagonia's distinct political life.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Political history is broadly attested through classical sources, but the territorial extent of the Paphlagonian kingdom at specific dates is only roughly defined.
